texts.preamble: Madan Lal Dawar vs Food Inspector on 8 April, 2022 The Court Of Shri Anil Antil Additional Sessions Judge-04, New Delhi District Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal Number : 65/2017 Unique Case Id No. 02403R0003832002 Cc No. : 99/02 (39687/16) U/S: : 16(1A) of P.F.A Act-1954 Madan Lal Dawar s/o Sh. Om Prakash r/o M-62, Majnu Ka Tila, Delhi-110054. .....Appellant versus Food Inspector, Department of Pfa, Govt of Nct of Delhi, A-20 Lawrence Road, Industrial Area, Delhi 110035. .....Respondent Appeal received by Predecessor Court on : 11.04.2017
texts.facts: Benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C, if any, applicable was also given to him. 3. The brief facts of the present case are that on 20.04.2002 the Food Inspectors Sh. Virendra Singh and Sh P N Khatri under the supervision of Local Health Authority/SDM Sh. V Valte along with staff reached at the premises of M/s Madan Store at shop no. 9, near Bus stop, Timarpur, Delhi-110054 where accused Madan Lal Dawar, Vendor cum Proprietor, of the said firm was found conducting business of various food articles including 'Dal Arhar' which were lying stored/exposed for sale for human consumption, in open plastic bag having no label declaration ; - that FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of commodity from the vendor which was lying in an open polythene bag bearing no label declaration, to which he agreed ; CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 2 of 9 - that thereafter as per the prescribed procedure under the PFA Act and Rules after giving notice to the vendor/appellant and offer towards the sale price of sample, to which he agreed and accepted the sale consideration, sample was then lifted ; - that each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked, sealed and necessary documents including Notice as per Form-VI in the presence of appellant/accused alongwith Panchnama proceedings etc was prepared at the spot ; - that thereafter one counterpart of sample was sent to Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA ; - that vide report dated 01.05.2002, the PA found the sample to be adulterated on the ground that it was coloured with synthetic colouring matter "Tartrazine" ; - that upon receipt of report, SDM/LHA directed investigation which was carried out by Food Inspector and after completion of investigation sanction under Section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 08.11.2002, against the appellant (vendor cum proprietor) alleging violation of Section 2(ia),(j) and (m) of PFA Act r/w Rules 23, 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, as punishable under Section 7/16(1A) of PFA. Act. Madan Lal Dawar vs Food Inspector on 8 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146237763/ 2 4. That the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, hence, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned by the learned trial court vide order dated 08.11.2002 to face trial. However, during the course of argument on 06.10.2021, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant does not wish to contest the present petition on merits, and the benefit of new legislation be given to the appellant; in this regard, on behalf of the appellant, an affidavit was also filed, mentioning that he is not challenging the merits of the case/ conviction decided by the learned trial court vide judgment dated 27.03.2017, and is confining it limited to the quantum of sentence only as awarded to him vide order dated 30.03.2017, and prayed that a lenient view be taken against him by giving him the benefit of New Legislation FSSAI.
texts.arguments: 6. It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that on the date of pronouncement of judgment/order on sentence, the PFA Act, 1954 was CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 4 of 9 repealed and new act had come into operation. It is stated that the court should give benefit of the new legislation to the accused vide which the punishment provided under the old act has been diluted to a considerable extent, and that the offence for which the accused/appellant has been convicted now falls under the category of "Unsafe Food" punishable under section 59(1) of the new Act i.e Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called FSSAI) punishable upto six months and fine of upto Rs. One lac only, and the minimum sentence provided in the earlier act has also been done away with. 7. It was argued by learned counsel for the appellant/convict that appellant is senior citizen aged about 66 years, suffering from paralysis and various ailments and thereby is not able to move and follow his daily routine work; that he has no source of income and the shop in question herein was also closed permanently way back about 15 years ago; that as of now due to his financial as well as Madan Lal Dawar vs Food Inspector on 8 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146237763/ 3 precarious medical condition, he is totally dependent upon his daughter with whom he is residing presently; that appellant has clean antecedents, not involved in any other case of similar nature or otherwise. 7.1 Further, it was submitted that the case pertains to the year 2002, the appellant/accused has faced the trial of almost 20 years, which by itself is a sufficient punishment in light of the fact that the hardship faced by the appellant during the said period has caused a great mental agony and stress not only to him but his entire family. It is also stated that now a days special circumstances exists due to outbreak of pandemic of Covid- 19 and there are chances of appellant being infected with virus in case imprisonment of sentence is awarded to him, and thereby it is prayed that a lenient view be taken against him in the light of the provisions of law under the new Act. CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 5 of 9 7.2 In support of his submissions qua the benefit of new legislation, learned counsel for appellant has relied upon the judgment of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No. 214 and 215 of 2016, vide order dated 10.03.2016, as corrected vide order dated 17.03.2016, as reported in 2016 (1) FAC 203 ) of Hon'ble Supreme Court and earlier judgment T Barai Vs. Henry 1983 ( ) SCC 177. 7.3 Per contra, learned SPP, strongly opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel by addressing that the sentencing cannot be done under new Act since the definition of many offences have changed in the new Act including this particular offence of which appellant/accused is charged. Definition of major offences like "adulteration" and "misbranding" have been changed. Now FSSAI has definitions of "substandard food", "food containing extraneous matter" "unsafe food" and misbranded food". Due to this reason, the ingredients have changed and thus there is no way in which the old offences could be related to new offences. 7.4 The application of Nemi Chand Judgment (supra), the same is based on the old judgment i.e. T Barai ( Supra) of Hon'ble Supreme Court. The relevant portion of the T Barai Judgment is as follows : - (Para 25) It is settled both on authority and principle that when a later statute again describes an offence created by an earlier statute and imposes a different punishment or varies the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by implication in Michell Vs. Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80 Lord Campbell put the matter thus : - "It is well settled rule of construction that, if a later statute again describes an offence created by a former statute and affixes a different punishment, varying the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by the later statute see also Smith Vs. Benabo ( 1937) 1 ALL ER 523 : ( 1997) 1 CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 6 of 9 KB 518: 156 LT 194" - In Regina Vs. Youle ( 1861) 158 ER 311,315-16 : LT 299 : 9 WR 637 Martin B. said in the oft-quoted passage : Madan Lal Dawar vs Food Inspector on 8 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146237763/ 4 - If a statute deals with a particular class of offences, and a subsequent Act is passed which deals with precisely the same offence, and a different punishment is imposed by the later Act, I think that, in effect, the legislature has declared that the new Act shall be substituted for the earlier Act." - The rule is however subject to the limitation contained in Article 20(1) against ex post facto law providing for a greater punishment and has also no application where the offence described in the later Act is not the same as in the earlier Act i.e. when the essential ingredients of the two offences are different. - Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows : - Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows : - To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life, then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases. Vide said letter the said authority, in the light of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's Case (supra) issued an advisory to the Commissioners of Food Safety/Officers incharge of Food Safety to dispose of the long CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 7 of 9 pending court cases filed under old PFA Act mainly concerning substandard and misbranding by imposing fine only.
